items.title: Earth atmosphere emulators could enable faster and more accurate weather predictions
items.excerpt: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory researchers, with DOE, NVIDIA and Los Alamos, train deep neural-network emulators such as STRATA on output from the physics-based E3SM model so they can predict atmospheric states without solving the equations; ML emulators for cloud microphysics and turbulence (STITCH) are also in development.

items.title: A sweeter future? AI helps scientists discover new sugar substitutes
items.excerpt: Hebrew University of Jerusalem researchers built a computational framework combining AI and molecular modeling that screened more than 50 million compounds and identified 92 promising sugar-substitute candidates (Food Chemistry).

items.title: AlphaFold 3 predicts complex immune interactions using protein sequences alone
items.excerpt: TGen (City of Hope) researchers developed an approach using AlphaFold 3 to predict whether a T cell receptor will recognize a specific antigen from its genetic sequence alone, which could speed decoding of immune responses to infections and tumors.

items.title: AI learns to predict the world without ever seeing it
items.excerpt: A Tel Aviv University and Stanford study asks whether a system can develop general learning capabilities without any exposure to real-world data, training models on synthetic inputs instead of books, images and recordings.

items.title: Let there be light: novel AI framework runs on optical hardware
items.excerpt: University of Tokyo-led researchers developed a new approach to physics-based AI, which uses the natural behavior of physical systems to process information, dramatically reducing required computation and demonstrated on optical hardware.

history_match.title: A new approach to sustainable AI: Offloading part of the computational burden onto light

items.title: SYNAPS-I: Intelligent computing transforms X-ray imaging, from data collection to discovery
items.excerpt: At DOE user facilities, researchers are building machine learning directly into X-ray experiments, using it to decide what to measure, reconstruct images as data arrive and rapidly extract scientific information.

history_match.title: Agentic AI turns simple language into self-guided X-ray scans of microelectronics

items.title: Exoplanets Can't Hide From The JWST's 'Digital Twin'
items.excerpt: FLIP (Physics-based Learning for Imaging Planets) builds a differentiable 'digital twin' of JWST's optics, borrowing machine-learning optimization to strip starlight far more precisely and reveal a giant planet hidden in two-year-old data.

history_match.title: Hybrid Digital Twins Developed for Future Autonomous Labs

items.title: AI helps Stanford scientists discover a 'natural Ozempic' with a surprising advantage
items.excerpt: Stanford researchers used AI to identify BRP, a natural peptide that cut food intake by up to 50% in animals via a different brain pathway than GLP-1 drugs, without the usual digestive side effects or major muscle loss.

items.title: Bird Flu Vaccine Developed Using AI Outperforms Current Stockpiled Vaccines in Preclinical Tests
items.excerpt: An AI-designed broad H5 influenza vaccine, DVX-panH5Nx, outperformed vaccines currently stockpiled by governments in preclinical studies. (Vaccine design; medicine boundary for curator.)

items.title: AI agents run this automated biology lab that sequences DNA and more
items.excerpt: A self-driving lab in China run by LLM agents needs only a simple prompt to encode messages in DNA and read them out; the accompanying Nature paper describes an AI-native lab for autonomous biomolecular operations. (Off-list exception: no on-list coverage.)

items.title: An open structure-guided RNA foundation model for generalizable prediction
items.excerpt: structRFM, an open RNA foundation model pre-trained on 21 million sequence-structure pairs, improves secondary and tertiary structure prediction, functional inference and zero-shot generalization. (Off-list exception: no on-list coverage.)

items.title: How 'reverse game theory' could keep AI agents in check
items.excerpt: AI safety researchers are borrowing mechanism design from economics to control AI agents' behavior through incentives, even without understanding the models' internals.

items.title: Could AI ever build itself? Scientists map the road to the 'last AI built by humans.'
items.excerpt: Researchers map how recursive self-improvement could let AI systems automate AI research itself to curb soaring development costs, and weigh whether it is viable.

items.title: Is AI making you lazier?
items.excerpt: A new study found people who relied on AI for basic tasks such as math problems became less motivated over time; Live Science polled readers on the findings.

items.title: Regina Barzilay and Jim Collins win Pritzker Prize for AI and Science Research Excellence
items.excerpt: MIT professors Regina Barzilay and Jim Collins received the Pritzker Prize for AI and Science Research Excellence for their work in AI-enabled antibiotic discovery.

items.title: How to tell if a voice recording is AI-generated
items.excerpt: A reporter clones her own voice in seconds and walks through the acoustic and perceptual cues, and the detection research, that help tell real speech from AI-generated audio.
